Cross-validation, including nested cross-validation, is a powerful tool for model evaluation and hyperparameter tuning, but it does NOT DIRECTLY ADDRESS data leakage. Data leakage refers to a situation where information from the test dataset leaks into the training dataset, causing the model to have an unrealistically high performance. Nested cross-validation can indeed help provide a more accurate estimation of the model's performance on unseen data, but IT DOESN'T SOLVE the underlying issue of data leakage if it's already present.
